name: Granada War, Final Reconquista Campaign
summary: Ferdinand II of Aragon and Isabella I of Castile launch the systematic conquest of the Nasrid Emirate of Granada, the last Muslim state in Iberia. The 10-year campaign uses artillery to reduce one castle at a time, avoiding pitched battles. The emirate's internal civil war (between Boabdil and his uncle Muhammad XIII) assists the conquest. Granada surrenders on January 2, 1492, the same year Columbus sails west.

_quarry.structural_significance: The fall of Granada closes the 781-year medieval Reconquista; its completion in the same year as Columbus's voyage is not coincidental, the Reconquista's resources, military experience, and ideological framework (holy war, conquest, conversion) are immediately transferred to the Americas; the expulsion of Spanish Jews (the Alhambra Decree, April 1492) follows within months, demonstrating that the Catholic Monarchs' religious uniformity project extends beyond military conquest
